# An @input handler that writes the var its input shows, with a different
# value, runs once per input -- the interpreter's reading. On gtk4 the write
# set the entry's text from inside its own "changed" emission, which emitted
# "changed" again, whose handler wrote again: the recursion ended in a SIGSEGV
# in EditableSetText. A program write to an entry's text is not user input,
# so it is made with "changed" blocked.

[!exec:pkg-config] skip 'pkg-config required'
[!gtk4] skip 'gtk4 development libraries required'
[!display] skip 'gtk4 runs its tests against a real GDK display (headless CI has none)'

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

component editor node {
    var s = ""
    var edits = 0
    input #field(
        value=s,
        @input(e) {
            s = e.value + "!"
            edits = edits + 1
        },
    )
}

func testRewriteRunsOnce(t Test, c editor) {
    c.field.input({value="h"})
    t.assert(c.s == "h!")
    t.assert(c.edits == 1)
}

window {
}
